Then Nebuchadnezzar returned to Babylon,
and made the hanging garden, called kremastos, that is, suspended,
and he made it to be one of the seven wonders.
And in the thirteenth year of the captivity, he made a golden image sixty cubits in height,
on account of which the house of Hananiah were glorified.
Then he became a beast according to the prophecy of Daniel,
and he grazed on grass with the beasts in the field.
And in this same time the gymnastic contest (gymnastikos?),
that is, of those who are naked,
began and became known in Athens.
And in the time of this Nebuchadnezzar there was also known Hipparchus the mathematical philosopher,
who, more than all the wise men who preceded him, took care concerning the observations and sight-lines of the movements of the zodiacal constellations.
And from his writings Ptolemy Claudius, the author of the book of the Almagest, which he titled the Syntaxis, was enlightened and strengthened.
And of the multitude of the books of Hipparchus, only one book is found today,
concerning the luminous mysteries from which are known the births (?) {OCR?} of the various kingdoms in the world. ... [Evil-Merodach] reigned {OCR?} three years after his father died,
and not after he lost his reason.
When this man reigned, he released Jehoiachin, who is Jeconiah, that is, Coniah, son of Jehoiakim, who is Eliakim, from prison and honored him.
And he ate bread before him at his table in the thirty-seventh year of his captivity,
which is the twenty-sixth year of the burning [of the Temple. And after him reigned Nergal-sharezer his brother {OCR?}] two years,
and according to the temple (?) {OCR?}.
After Evil-Merodach ... of the Chaldeans, five {OCR?}.
In his first year Daniel saw the vision of the four beasts,
which signified the four kingdoms.
And that Belshazzar,
in his second year,
made a great banquet for his nobles,
and he drank wine before the thousand;
that is, in their presence, and not like them.
And when he dared to drink from the vessels of ministry which his father had captured,
the palm of a hand came forth and wrote his sentence on the wall.
And on that very night Darius the Mede came and killed him.
